title: San Francisco → Tokyo — late November 2026
example_notice: This is a baked-in EXAMPLE report with fictional data (a made-up SFO→Tokyo search) shipped so the site always has something to show. Not a real Devon trip.

search_params.label: Route(s)
search_params.value: SFO ⇄ Tokyo NRT — round-trip (open-jaw NRT-in / HND-out also checked)

search_params.label: Dates searched
search_params.value: Flexible window: depart Nov 20–23, return Nov 30–Dec 3 2026 (date-matrix swept)

search_params.label: Cabins
search_params.value: 2 economy + 2 business (mixed; business confirmed as a hard requirement for the 2 premium travelers)

recommendation:
Book the round-trip SFO⇄NRT: ANA nonstop for the 2 business travelers (~$4,180/seat via Ignav, matched within $40 on Google Flights) and United/ZIPAIR for the 2 economy travelers (~$690/seat).

Skip the positioning-flight play — the modeled saving (~$430/business seat) is well under Devon's $1,000 business-class threshold, and it isn't worth the separate-ticket risk on a 4-person family trip.

Strongly consider burning miles for the two business seats instead of cash: Seats.aero shows Qantas/Aeroplan award space at ~167k miles + ~$366 taxes per J seat on Nov 22 — that's dramatically better value than the ~$4,180 cash fare if the miles are available.
recommendation_reasoning:
Cash business is genuinely expensive this window and the cheapest cash source (Ignav) only undercut Google Flights by ~$40 — no meaningful cash arbitrage between the two markets tried.

The award layer is where the real money is: two J seats at 167k miles each is the classic premium-cabin points-crush-cash case, and it fits Devon's transferable-points profile. The catch is award space is volatile — it must be grabbed fast, so treat it as a 'decide now' option rather than something to sit on.

Open-jaw (NRT-in / HND-out) came in essentially flat versus the round-trip baseline here, so there's no reason to add itinerary complexity for it.

source_comparison.headline: 167,000 mi + $366
source_comparison.detail: Award space open Nov 22 — points value beats the ~$4,180 cash fare

cheapest_note: Cheapest CASH per cabin is highlighted. The Seats.aero row is AWARD (points) data, not cash — shown as a cross-check, not a like-for-like price.

market_arbitrage.summary: Tried the US (departure) and JP (destination) markets. Difference was marginal — under 1% on both cabins — so no market arbitrage win on this route this window. Did NOT try a 3rd market (would ask Devon first).

date_matrix.summary: Swept departures Nov 20–23 against returns Nov 30–Dec 3 (economy fare used as the mover). Cheapest pair was depart Sat Nov 21 / return Tue Dec 1 — ~$120/economy seat cheaper than the mid-week-out / weekend-back pair.
date_matrix.best_pair: Depart Sat Nov 21 → Return Tue Dec 1 2026

open_jaw.summary: Tokyo has two viable gateways (NRT and HND), so open-jaw was worth checking. Fly into NRT, out of HND came in within ~$25/seat of the plain round-trip into NRT — essentially flat. No reason to add complexity; recommending the straight round-trip.
open_jaw.roundtrip_baseline: Round-trip SFO⇄NRT — economy $690 / business $4,180 per seat (baseline).
open_jaw.openjaw_option: Open-jaw SFO→NRT, HND→SFO — economy ~$715 / business ~$4,205 per seat. ~$25 higher; not worth it here.

hub_hacking.summary: Modeled a positioning play: cheap SFO→LAX leg, then a discounted ex-LAX business fare to NRT. It penciled out to roughly $430/business-seat saving versus booking straight from SFO.
hub_hacking.threshold_note: Below Devon's $1,000-business-class positioning-flight threshold ($430 < $1,000), so NOT recommended. Mentioned only for completeness.
risk_caveats: Separate tickets = NO through-checked bags; reclaim and recheck at LAX.
NO airline rebooking protection across separate tickets — if the SFO→LAX leg is delayed and the LAX→NRT departure is missed, that long-haul seat may have to be re-bought outright.

Buffer-time rule: a same-day positioning leg needs 4–6+ hours of slack minimum; for a high-value business itinerary, arriving LAX the day before is the safer call — especially on a low-cost-carrier positioning leg.

hidden_city_note: Not applicable / not recommended for this trip — it's a round-trip, and hidden-city/throwaway ticketing only ever works one-way or as a final segment, voids the remainder of the ticket the moment a segment is skipped, carries frequent-flyer account-ban risk, and can't through-check bags. Flagged here only so the omission is explicit.
footer_note: Cash prices are point-in-time and expire fast; award space is volatile. Re-verify before booking.
